notes: 161st Regimental Combat Team landed on 4 January 1943, completing the 25th Division’s landing; all units landed without loss (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). Confidence 0.7.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, 25th Division's Preliminary Movements
current_activity: making the 25th Division's main effort south-west of the Galloping Horse
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: Collins's 20 January order gave the 161st Infantry (Colonel Orndorff) the division's main effort on 22 January, to seize the small open hills south-west of Hill 53 and then move north-west through the jungle toward Hill 87. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. The regiment is not given a Kokumbona pin of its own; Miller names the 27th Infantry as the unit that entered the village the next day.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: passing through the 147th and reaching the Umasani River by 2020
notes: Miller, ch. XV: the 161st Infantry, then commanded by Colonel James L. Dalton II, passed through the 147th about 1000 on 6 February 1943. By 2020 it had reached the Umasani River, and patrols had crossed. The day's only skirmish was a patrol fight on a ridge just west of the river. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal
current_activity: driving the Japanese from the Tambalego and advancing to Doma Cove
notes: Miller, ch. XV: the 161st Infantry encountered some Japanese at the Tambalego River on 8 February 1943, but after a brief fight drove them off and advanced to Doma Cove. On 7 February it had already crossed the Umasani and advanced to Bunina. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal; R2226: ch. IX, The Final Drive
current_activity: entering Tenaro and meeting 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry
notes: Miller, ch. XV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that on 9 February 1943 the north-coast and south-coast American forces met near Cape Esperance, ending organised fighting. Miller writes that 1st Battalion, 161st Infantry, passed through the 3rd Battalion at Doma Cove, marched about five miles, crossed the Tenamba, and entered Tenaro, where between 1600 and 1700 it met 2nd Battalion, 132nd Infantry. Confidence 0.7.
